extra.prompt:
Predictable Code found this defect and I want it fixed:

  A value in this function may be null where it is used
  Function: parse.tidy
  Location: scripts/render/parse.mjs:94
  Kind: callee-precondition (Reachable from current code)
  Stable id: FIN-0055
  Descriptor: Code.scripts.render.parse.tidy|il1.null-dereference
A value in this function may be null where it is used. This function uses a value that is expected to be present, and the analysis could not rule out its being null at that point.

Tracked as requirement SPEC-009/ANL-0028: `parse.tidy` requires that the value of `at`(`out`, -1) is not null.
Is it fixed? Run, from the repository root:
  predictable fix-check --key 'Code.scripts.render.parse.tidy|il1.null-dereference' --json

Fix the underlying cause in the source.
Do NOT delete or disable the code, and do NOT weaken an existing check —
either would make the defect disappear without fixing anything.

Keep the specs true to the code you leave behind. If your change alters what a function
accepts, returns, throws or guarantees — or you take any other code action that does — update,
in the same change, the spec pages that describe it (the Markdown spec files Predictable Code
discovered in this repository; `predictable specs list` names them) and any documentation of
that behaviour (README sections, doc comments, docs pages). Never edit a spec to make a defect
disappear: a spec states the intended behaviour, and the code must meet it.

You are not done until the analysis agrees. Before you started, Predictable Code recorded
the project as it stands — this defect and everything else the analysis reports
(its "findings": every row it reports — defects, and the checks it could not decide or that hold by design).
Never run `fix-check --start` yourself: it would record your changes as that starting point.
Work like this, until it is done:
  1. Change the source.
  2. Run the "Is it fixed?" command. It runs `predictable sync`,
     which can take several minutes: run it in the foreground and wait for it to exit.
  3. Read its `verdict`:
     - `gone`: fixed and verified. You are done.
     - `reported`: still reported. Read the source again and try a different fix.
     - `regressed`: gone, but your change added findings (named in `introduced`) or the
       analysis's total did not go down. A fix must leave FEWER findings than it found:
       keep working on the code — or on its specs, where the intended behaviour changed —
       until nothing new is reported.
     - `not-analysed`: the function was not analysed (renamed, removed, or its file no
       longer translates). Keep its name and make it translate again.
     - `sync-failed`: the analysis did not run; its `reason` says why.
There is no round limit. After every turn Predictable Code runs this same check itself and
sends you back with its verdict until it reads `gone`, so stopping early only costs a turn.
The "Is it fixed?" command is the only check: never run `predictable sync` yourself.
Never stop while a sync is still running.

End your last message with one line:
  RESULT: fixed
or
  RESULT: not fixed — <why you could not fix it>
Nothing is proposed for review unless the analysis no longer reports it.

You are in the project's own working tree, on its current branch. No other
fix is running: they run one at a time, never concurrently.
Do not switch or merge branches, and leave your changes uncommitted so they
can be reviewed as a diff.
